stem: Ciprofloxacin is used to treat or prevent which of the following sets of infections?

options.label: A
options.text: Syphilis, Lyme disease and streptococcal pharyngitis
options.misconception: Assumes a broad-spectrum antibiotic covers every bacterial infection, including spirochetes and streptococci.
options.explanation: Syphilis, Lyme disease and strep pharyngitis are treated with penicillin, doxycycline or amoxicillin; ciprofloxacin is not an effective choice for any of them.

options.label: B
options.text: Typhoid fever, infectious diarrhea and osteomyelitis
options.misconception: None — ciprofloxacin treats certain bacterial infections such as typhoid and infectious diarrhea.
options.explanation: MedlinePlus lists ciprofloxacin for certain bacterial infections, including pneumonia, typhoid fever, infectious diarrhea and skin, bone and joint infections.

options.label: C
options.text: Oral thrush, tinea pedis and aspergillosis
options.misconception: Assumes a broad-spectrum antibiotic also covers fungal infections.
options.explanation: Thrush, tinea pedis and aspergillosis are fungal infections treated with antifungals; ciprofloxacin has no antifungal activity.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Assumes a fluoroquinolone's antibacterial spectrum extends to protozoa.
options.explanation: Malaria, giardiasis and toxoplasmosis are protozoal infections that need antiprotozoal drugs, not a fluoroquinolone antibacterial.

options.label: E
options.text: Clostridioides difficile colitis, anaerobic lung abscess and actinomycosis
options.misconception: Assumes any bacterial infection responds to ciprofloxacin, overlooking its weak anaerobic coverage.
options.explanation: Fluoroquinolones predispose to C. difficile colitis, which needs oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin; ciprofloxacin also lacks the anaerobic coverage abscess and actinomycosis need.

context: Learning objective: Ciprofloxacin treats or prevents certain bacterial infections, such as pneumonia, typhoid fever, infectious diarrhea and skin, bone and joint infections.
